item.title: [Itrfoundation] The Cost of Leading Iowa Counties
item.description:
An Analysis of Supervisor Pay, Board Size, and Taxpayer Cost

County supervisors in Iowa adopt budgets, set property tax levies, oversee public safety, and maintain secondary roads. And while Iowa counties operate under the same basic legal framework, they do not all govern themselves in a uniform manner.  In fact, Iowa’s home rule law gives counties broad flexibility in carrying out those duties, as long as their actions do not conflict with the Iowa Constitution or state law. 

For instance, a county may have three supervisors or five and it may classify its supervisors as full-time or part-time. Even the salaries that are paid to these county leaders are left up to each county to decide, as state law only law establishes the process for setting compensation; it does not impose a uniform minimum or maximum supervisor salary.

Those choices all affect what residents ultimately pay for the their County Supervisors. This brief uses the Iowa State Association of Counties (ISAC) fiscal year 2026 salary survey to examine supervisor salaries, board structure, employment classifications, salary changes, and taxpayer costs across Iowa to consider a broader question: How much are Iowans paying for county leadership?

The post The Cost of Leading Iowa Counties appeared first on ITR Foundation.
